errata.original: candidate cap of 4 per cycle reached (safety limit)
errata.correction: The 4-candidate cap was set for the implementing session's wall time (protocols/abc-real-1.json notes), not as a safety limit. The user forbade time- or cost-motivated low limits. The search never reached its no-progress stop: the run is truncated exploratory evidence. Only 3 candidates per arm were evaluated (the 4th was left in screening by a boundary bug fixed later).

errata.original: Q columns report the Monte Carlo mean of the task-level bootstrap as the point estimate
errata.correction: Exact empirical rates (final attempt per unit): stable dev 37/48 = 77.0833%, pure dev 43/48 = 89.5833%, multi3 dev 46/48 = 95.8333%, B-c001 dev 37/48 = 77.0833% (identical to stable), C-c001 dev 38/48 = 79.1667%, stable holdout 15/21 = 71.4286%, C-c001 holdout 13/21 = 61.9048%. protocol-2 uses exact plug-in points.

errata.original: multi3 presented as the baseline that separates extra compute from harness effects
errata.correction: multi3 allows up to 3 pure-Pi attempts per unit but used exactly 1 attempt in all 48 dev units (432 requests vs stable 917; input tokens 0.18x). It is a second single-attempt sample of pure Pi, not an equal-compute or opportunity-matched control.

errata.original: C-c001 development-qualified and selected (protocol-1 relative integrity rule)
errata.correction: All of C-c001's violations were task-agent edits of existing test files (no leak, route violation, crash or patch violation): 3 screening runs, 5 dev runs (stable 5), 2 development-train runs (unchecked by protocol-1), 8 holdout runs (stable 4). protocol-2 treats any such run as critical regardless of the baseline and would have rejected C-c001 at screening.

errata.original: holdout-v1 used once by this run
errata.correction: holdout-v1 is implementer-authored and consumed. It is not independent, is not reused for tuning, and was neither loaded nor shown to the optimizer in explore-real-2.
